questions.question: Which of the following is a good, strong password?
choices: A series of numbers, letters, and special characters that you can remember
questions.explanation: A strong password should be difficult to guess but easy to remember. Include numbers and symbols, and remember that longer passwords are stronger.

questions.question: Who should you share your password with?
questions.explanation: Never share your passwords with anyone except trusted adults like your parents.

questions.question: When browsing the internet, you should avoid which of the following?
choices: Downloading files from a website you're not familiar with
Reading articles on things you're interested in
questions.explanation: Always be careful downloading files online, and ensure the place you're downloading from is safe and trustworthy.

questions.question: Where is a safe place to download apps?
choices: The official app store on your device
A site you were recommended by a friend
Something you were recommended by an ad
It's not safe to download any apps, stick with what you have
questions.explanation: While not every app outside the app store is unsafe, generally you should stick to apps that have been approved by the official app store your device uses to stay secure.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help keep your device secure?
choices: Logging out of your device when you aren't using it
Writing down your password so you remember it
questions.explanation: It's generally not a good idea to write down passwords, as others might read them and figure out what your password is.

questions.question: Which of the following helps add extra security to your device?
choices: Never turn on WiFi on your device
Turn on auto fill for your passwords
questions.explanation: Two-factor authentication adds an extra method of verifying your identity on top of a password and helps keep your device extra secure.

questions.question: Which of the following should you be careful connecting to?
choices: A public WiFi router at a restaurant
questions.explanation: You should always be careful connecting to networks you don't recognize, as many are insecure and can expose your device to danger.

questions.question: What is the process of making data unreadable by humans to protect it called?
questions.explanation: Encryption uses mathematical processes to turn readable text and data into unreadable strings of characters so it stays protected while being sent.

questions.question: What should you do when you're done using a public computer on your account?
questions.explanation: Always log out of all your accounts when you're done using public computers, as anyone can sit down and gain access to your account if you don't.

questions.question: What should you do when your device is not currently using WiFi or Bluetooth?
choices: Shut your device down and don't use it
Leave WiFi or Bluetooth on all the time
Turn off WiFi or Bluetooth when they aren't being used
questions.explanation: Leaving Bluetooth and WiFi on while you're not using them can expose your device to threats, so turn them off when they're not being used.
